decisions.diagnosis: Counter 197 reported 0 in both directions for five months while riders kept passing; the counts were never recorded so they cannot be recovered.
decisions.evidence: Both directions 0 from 2019-04-28 evening until 2019-09-30 00:15 (3701 h); adjacent site 191 (10 m away) kept ~290-610 per day, e.g. 2019-04-29 191=304 vs 190=0, 2019-09-29 191=610 vs 190=0; 190 normally reads ~0.94x site 191.

decisions.diagnosis: Counter 197 reported 0 in both directions for three full days while the path was in normal use; the counts were not recorded and cannot be recovered.
decisions.evidence: Zeros 2022-05-15 22:00 to 2022-05-19 05:30 in both directions; site 191 368/413/399 and 187 458/511/498 on the same days; normal counts resume 2022-05-19 06:00.

decisions.diagnosis: Counter 299 reported 0 (warning status) in both directions for 11 days over Christmas while riders kept passing; the counts cannot be recovered.
decisions.evidence: Zeros 2024-12-23 23:15/23:45 to 2025-01-04 00:00; adjacent site 191 recorded 272-734 per day (e.g. 12-31: 734) while 190 had 0; 190 tracked 191 at ~0.94 immediately before and after.

decisions.diagnosis: A midnight-to-midnight day of warning-status zeros shared with the separate counters at sites 191 and 195 looks like a data outage filled with zeros, not a real absence of riders.
decisions.evidence: 190, 191 and 195 all exactly 0 on Monday 2025-10-20, zeros aligned to 00:00-24:00, status warning; site 124 on the same river path recorded 623; the neighbouring days were 752 and 448 at 190.

decisions.diagnosis: Counter 299's sensor failed from 1 March 2026 until it was replaced by counter 391 on 22 April: direction 1087 dropped to 5-40% of normal and 1088 swung between large overcounts and undercounts, so neither the split nor the total can be trusted or recovered.
decisions.evidence: Before March the 1087/1088 totals ran at 0.92-0.95x site 191 and 1087 about equal to 1088; from 2026-03-01 1087 = 6-138 per day against 191's 150-340 per direction; 1088 = 418 on 03-06 and 383 on 03-08 (191: 187-224, 109-142), then 43-116 on weekdays from 03-23 (191: ~200-270); the site total ranged from 0.27x to 1.72x of 191; replacement counter 391 read 0.94-0.95x of 191 again from 2026-04-22.

series.name: North-east / North (towards the city)
series.evidence: The three counters replaced one another at the same site in sequence with no overlap. The weekday hourly profiles match: the peak is at 08:00 with a weaker 07:00 (192: 9.3/15.9; 1088: 12.2/20.3; 1857: 10.5/16.3), and 15:00 is lower than in the other direction. The 299 and 391 labels (North) agree with each other. Each counter's site total reads a steady ~0.93-0.96x of adjacent site 191, so their levels are comparable.

series.name: South-west / South (away from the city)
series.evidence: The three counters replaced one another in sequence. The weekday profiles match: 07:00 is at or above 08:00 (201: 13.4/11.6; 1087: 18.4/14.7; 1859: 14.3/13.1), and 15:00 is stronger than in the other direction. The 299 and 391 labels (South) agree. The levels against site 191 are stable across the counter changes.

summary: Site 190 on the Parramatta River north bank tracks adjacent site 191 closely (about 0.94x) across all three counters, so three direction pairs of counter replacements form two continuous series. The faults are counter 197 reporting zeros from May to September 2019 and on 16-18 May 2022, counter 299 reporting zeros over Christmas 2024/25, a shared outage day on 20 October 2025, and counter 299's sensor failing in March-April 2026 before its replacement; all are set missing. Other short zero days (Feb 2020, Jul 2020, Mar 2021, Aug 2021, Feb/Mar/Jul 2022, Apr 2024) match the neighbours and are real weather or flooding lows.
